hook: The painter of grace and harmony, who died at 37 at the height of his fame.

pages.x: Raffaello Sanzio was born in 1483 in Urbino, the son of the court painter. Orphaned at 11, he trained with the painter Perugino and soon outshone him.
In Florence he studied Leonardo and Michelangelo, and painted a series of gentle Madonnas with the baby Jesus and little John the Baptist that made him famous.

In 1508 Pope Julius II hired him, at 25, to paint rooms in the Vatican. In The School of Athens he gathered the great thinkers of Greece in a vast hall: Plato has the face of Leonardo, and Raphael himself peeps out at the edge.

A story says his friend Bramante let him sneak into the Sistine Chapel to see Michelangelo's half-finished ceiling. Raphael then added a brooding figure in Michelangelo's style to his School of Athens. Michelangelo grumbled that everything Raphael knew, he had learned from him.

His Sistine Madonna shows Mary stepping down through the clouds with the baby Jesus. At the bottom, two bored little angels lean on their elbows; they have become two of the most copied images in the world, on everything from stamps to umbrellas.
He became chief architect of St Peter's and ran a large workshop. He died on Good Friday 1520, his 37th birthday, after a short fever, and was buried in the Pantheon.
With Leonardo and Michelangelo, Raphael is one of the three giants of the High Renaissance. His calm, balanced pictures were the model for painters for 400 years.
